newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Feb 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Feb 24.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Before entry of a strategic partner into Agrobanka during compulsory administration, the bank's losses of 8.7 billion crowns must be balanced. In its search for a solution, the Czech National Bank gives preference to an agreement with the most influential shareholders in the bank, which are represented by Motoinvest Group.

- Last week, the workers union in Poldi announced its readiness to strike, because workers are not receiving their wages. According to the chairman of the union, Josef Kotouc, workers are owed around 100 million crowns.

- Credit Suisse First Boston decreased its original estimation of Komercni Banka's profits for last year in its February analysis, because contrary to previous expectations, the bank is continuing to create reserves for bad loans.

- The state fund for market regulation has changed the way in which it will intervene on the grain market this year and next year. At the end of last week, it announced a minimum guaranteed price for wheat, which will progressively increase each month.

PRAVO - The holding company Chemopol Group no longer intends to use its right to 25 percent of Kaucuk's shares, which was approved by the cabinet in 1993. Rather than merging with Kaucuk into Unipetrol Group as the cabinet planned, Chemapol plans to build its own industrial group, independent of Unipetrol.
- Government investment in a program to restore the housing fund will be about one third of what is actually needed, according to Regional Development Minister Jaromir Schneider.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - The medical physicians union announced that doctors will not go on strike. They state that health services lack about 16 billion crowns. For this reason, the union proposes to increase health insurance from 13.5 percent to 14.5 percent.

- Kladno Energy Centre had losses last year of 25 million crowns, and its sales decreased from 1.25 billion to 760 million crowns. Milana Prajzlera, agent for the company, blames the results on the drastic decrease in energy consumption from the second largest customer, Poldi metalworks.

LIDOVE NOVINY - Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus ended a four-day official visit to Canada yesterday. During the trip, he gained Canada's support for the Czech Republic's entry into NATO, which was his main reason for going there.
